stem: The family of a client with advanced cancer and diagnosed cachexia says, 'If we can just make him eat enough calories, the muscle loss should reverse.' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Cachexia is a complex wasting syndrome that is not fully reversed by nutrition alone; care should address symptoms and medical contributors while using individualized nutrition support, often with a registered dietitian.
options.B: Cachexia is caused only by inadequate calorie intake, so increasing food intake is sufficient to reverse the syndrome in most clients.
options.C: Nutrition support has no role in cachexia, so dietary assessment and symptom-related eating problems should not be addressed.
options.D: Every client with cachexia should receive the same high-calorie meal plan regardless of appetite, symptoms, cancer type, or goals of care.

rationale: NCI describes cancer cachexia as a multifactorial wasting syndrome involving weakness and loss of skeletal muscle and fat that, unlike simple malnutrition, cannot be reversed with nutrition support alone. Inflammation and metabolic changes can contribute, along with reduced intake and treatment-related symptoms. Management is individualized and multidisciplinary. Nutrition support remains useful: a registered dietitian can assess needs and recommend strategies such as small frequent meals, higher-protein/higher-calorie foods, or supplements while the healthcare team addresses symptoms and other contributors. The goal is not to force one universal diet or to assume calories alone can reverse the underlying syndrome.
educational_objective: Differentiate cancer cachexia from simple inadequate intake and support individualized multidisciplinary management that includes, but is not limited to, nutrition intervention.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Cancer Cachexia; Nutrition in Cancer Care (PDQ®) — Health Professional Version
source_locator: Cancer Cachexia — definition, causes, and Ways to manage cancer cachexia; Nutrition in Cancer Care PDQ — Methods of Nutrition Therapy, counseling by a registered dietitian, loss-of-appetite/weight-loss strategies
source_claim_supported: NCI states that cancer cachexia causes muscle and fat loss and cannot be reversed by nutrition support alone. NCI supports multidisciplinary management and registered-dietitian counseling with individualized nutrition strategies for weight loss and eating problems.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — nutrition, feeding support, symptom-related eating problems, and individualized comfort-focused care
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — individualized nutrition support within multidisciplinary management of cancer cachexia
correction_summary: Rebuilt the original generic nutrition-plan item around the defining clinical distinction between cachexia and simple malnutrition. The final item explicitly prevents the misconception that increased calories alone reverse cachexia, while preserving an evidence-based role for individualized dietitian-guided nutrition and symptom management. Removed the implication that one universal calorie-dense diet is appropriate for every client.
audit_findings: Original item was broadly reasonable but risked making high-calorie intake sound like the central corrective treatment for a syndrome that is not reversed by nutrition alone.
Fresh NCI review directly distinguishes cachexia from malnutrition and describes inflammatory/metabolic mechanisms in addition to reduced intake.
The final item preserves the useful role of registered-dietitian support and practical nutrition strategies without promising reversal of cachexia.
No universal feeding route, supplement, calorie target, or medication is prescribed because management depends on symptoms, disease context and goals.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct explanation with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported nutritional guarantee, or unresolved source conflict.
